title: Dictionaries
short_description: Use key-value dictionaries to organize data.
bro_quote: Dictionaries turn chaos into order—key-value pairs make your data structured and accessible.

subtopics.name: Dictionary Basics
subtopics.explanation:
• 📚 A dictionary stores pairs of keys and values. Like a real dictionary: word (key) → definition (value).
  • 🔑 Use curly braces {} and colons : to create dictionaries.
  • ⚡ Keys must be unique and usually strings or numbers. Values can be anything.
  • 🚀 Lookup is super fast — dictionaries are optimized for this.
  • 🔄 Dictionaries are mutable — you can add, change, or remove pairs.

subtopics.name: Accessing Dictionary Values
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔑 Access values using keys in square brackets: dict[key]
  • ⚠️ Using a non-existent key causes a KeyError.
  • 🛡️ .get(key) safely retrieves values without crashing if key doesn't exist.
  • 💡 .get(key, default) returns a default value if key is missing.

snippets.code:
user = {"name": "Alice", "age": 25}
print(user["name"])           # Alice
print(user.get("email"))      # None
print(user.get("email", "N/A")) # N/A

subtopics.name: Modifying Dictionary Pairs
subtopics.explanation:
• ✏️ Change a value: dict[key] = new_value
  • ➕ Add a new pair: dict[new_key] = value
  • ❌ del dict[key] removes a pair.
  • 🗑️ .pop(key) removes and returns a value.
  • 🧹 .clear() removes all pairs.

snippets.code:
person = {"name": "Alice", "age": 25}
person["age"] = 26          # Update
person["city"] = "NYC"      # Add new
print(person)

subtopics.name: Dictionary Methods
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔑 .keys() returns all keys as a list.
  • 📊 .values() returns all values as a list.
  • 👥 .items() returns key-value pairs as tuples.
  • 🔍 'key' in dict checks if a key exists.
  • 🔄 .update(other_dict) merges two dictionaries.

subtopics.name: Iterating Through Dictionaries
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔑 Loop through keys: for key in dict
  • 👥 Loop through key-value pairs: for key, value in dict.items()
  • 📊 Loop through values only: for value in dict.values()
  • 💡 Use tuple unpacking to separate keys and values in loops.

subtopics.name: Nested Dictionaries
subtopics.explanation:
• 🎯 Dictionaries can contain other dictionaries as values.
  • 🏢 Great for organizing complex data structures.
  • 🔑 Access nested values: dict[key][nested_key]

questions: 1. Create a dictionary storing your name, age, and favorite color. (Creating dictionary)
2. Retrieve and print just the value associated with the 'name' key. (Accessing value)
3. Add a brand new key-value pair for 'hobby' to the dictionary. (Adding pair)
4. Update your existing 'age' value to make yourself one year older. (Updating value)
5. Use del or .pop() to completely remove the favorite color key. (Deleting pair)
6. Check if the key 'email' exists in the dictionary using the 'in' keyword. (Checking keys)
7. Print a list of all the keys currently in your dictionary. (Getting keys)
8. Print a list of all the values currently in your dictionary. (Getting values)
9. Use a for loop with .items() to print both keys and values together. (Iterating items)
10. Use the .get() method to try to fetch a key that might not exist without crashing. (Using get)
